html:
The Wangkangurru are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Simpson Desert, in the far north of South Australia. They also call themselves Nharla. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

The Simpson is a sea of long parallel red sand dunes with no rivers. The Wangkangurru lived there by knowing dozens of small wells, called mikiri, dug down to water held under the sand, and moved between them as each one ran low. On the desert's edges, mound springs fed by the Great Artesian Basin gave more water.

They kept living in the deep desert well into the colonial period. Around 1900, after drought and with stations and missions near its edges, the last groups walked out and settled on the fringes, some at the Lutheran mission at Killalpaninna. Linguists recorded their language with the last fluent speakers late in the 20th century. Neighbours on the map include the Karangura, the Ngamini and the Yarluyandi. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
